channels.cadence: once, when the page reports ready
channels.try: Type a pattern, close the plugin window, reopen it.
channels.expect: reopening the plugin window shows the pattern and settings you left, not defaults

channels.try: Type `E(1,8)>8` and press Enter about eight times, watching the wheel.
channels.expect: the wheel and step row show what the engine is playing, including after a progressive trigger
channels.notes: Change-detected. The scene-transform race (2026-07-29) was invisible here because the pattern genuinely was not changing — the transform was being overwritten before this ran.

channels.try: Press play. Then switch Host sync on and change the host's tempo.
channels.expect: the playhead moves while playing and the BPM readout follows the host

channels.try: Type `E(3,8)|E(3,8)*3/E(3,7)` and press Enter several times. Then do it again using MIDI notes instead of Enter.
channels.expect: each poly lane's row shows what that lane is sounding, its label names the scene it is on, and its playhead moves
channels.notes: The reason this tool exists. Emitted by C++ and handled by main.jsx for weeks with no juceOn subscription between them, so every event was dropped: lane playheads never moved and a scene chain displayed its first scene forever. Fixed 2026-07-30 (music-suite 193ebdf).

channels.try: Move the accent velocity slider. Then automate that same parameter from the host and watch the slider.
channels.expect: automating a parameter in the host moves the matching control, and moving the control writes automation

channels.cadence: on Enter, or any pattern edit
channels.try: Type `E(3,8)%2` and press Enter repeatedly. Then try `E(7,16)>16/E(1,17)>17`.
channels.expect: typing a pattern and pressing Enter changes what plays; re-entering the same chain advances it
channels.notes: The engine is authoritative: the raw text is sent without gating on the JS parser, which is why the UI can show a parse error for a string the engine handles. That mismatch cost hours on 2026-07-29.

channels.try: Turn Host sync off, then use the play and stop buttons in Serpe's own header.
channels.expect: play/stop in the plugin's own header starts and stops the sequencer when host sync is off
a pattern typed or triggered reaches the audio thread exactly once, and any rotation or lengthening survives the trip
channels.notes: Scene transforms lost this race for months: they were applied immediately after enqueue, so the queued base overwrote them. Only intermittently visible, as brief glimpses of the other scene. Fixed 2026-07-28 (Serpe 53df3ec).

channels.expect: each poly lane advances its own scene chain independently, so two scenes against three realign every six triggers
